newsitem.title: CHINA: Most urban Chinese want to buy own homes.
newsitem.headline: Most urban Chinese want to buy own homes.

text.p: Most urban Chinese residents plan to buy their own homes instead of waiting for their work units to allocate houses to them, the Overseas Edition of the People's Daily said on Monday.
About 53.07 percent of residents in urban areas intend to purchase their own homes while 29.27 percent said they did not want to buy, said a survey published in the newspaper.
The government survey showed home purchases tended to be influenced by job and salary.

More than 67 percent of private businessmen and employees of foreign-funded enterprises planned to buy homes while about 63.35 percent of people earning more than 25,000 yuan ($3,012) in annual income wanted to buy, the survey said.

Beijing's communist authorities first relaxed rules on ordinary Chinese buying their own homes in the late 1980s and early 1990s, and issued new rules in April making it easier for individuals to obtain mortgages to boost private home buying.
However, inadequate regulations and high risks for banks have hampered development of personal mortgage loans, said the China Business Daily.
Buying a home was still far out of the reach of ordinary Chinese wage-earners, the newspaper said.
An estimated 80 percent of China's 1.2 billion people live in its cities. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
